intent: Enterprise-grade, feature-first frontend core for Bulletproof React applications (React 19 + Vite SPA).

currentProjectSetup.ui: feature-owned UI with minimal shared primitives (no MUI dependency)

nonGoals: This file must not override codex.rules.json.
This file should not define new architecture if codex.rules.json already defines it.

ownershipMatrix: React Query owns all server-derived state (including authenticated User | null).
React Hook Form owns all form state.
React local state owns UI and interaction state only.
URL state belongs in React Router (params/search) and pages/** wiring.
Context is allowed only for minimal app-level UI state (theme, i18n, feature flags) and must not store server-derived data or duplicate React Query cache.
notes: Prefer feature-local UI state to preserve deletion safety.
Cross-feature UI state should be rare and must be justified.
antiPatterns: Duplicating React Query results into context, a store, or useState for global access.
Treating JWTs or tokens as frontend state (no persistent token storage).
Persisting access or refresh tokens in localStorage or sessionStorage.
Building global stores under shared/** as cross-feature dumping grounds.
Using shared/** to own feature domain state.

apiLayer.singleClientRule: Use the shared HTTP client only; no ad-hoc fetch/Axios instances.
apiLayer.featureOwnership: API modules live under features/<feature>/api/** by default; shared/** is infra only.
apiLayer.reactQueryOnlyConsumer: React Query is the only allowed consumer of API calls.
apiLayer.contracts: Zod v4 schemas own API contracts; derive types via z.input/z.output only.
apiLayer.errorHandling: API layer normalizes errors with no UI side effects.
antiPatterns: Global API services layers that erase feature ownership.
Calling API functions directly from components.

codingPrinciples: Organize code by business domain (features) rather than technical type.
Prefer feature-local solutions over global abstractions.
Frontend never invents business rules; backend is source of truth.
Validate data only at boundaries; trust validated data internally.
Static, reviewable UI over clever abstractions.

authUxPolicy: Login and credential errors are shown inline; do not toast them.
Unexpected auth failures may toast and redirect.
Do not move login errors into global handlers.
apiEnvelopeSupport: Support both envelope-based and status-code-based errors.
Do not assume { success: false } is universal.

accessibilityBaseline.description: Minimal accessibility baseline enforced for frontend implementation and scoped reviews.
required: Use semantic interactive elements: button, a, input, select, textarea, label, table, th.
Ensure keyboard operability for all interactive controls.
Preserve visible focus; do not suppress with focus:outline-none, focus:ring-0, or focus:shadow-none.
Set correct button type attributes and aria-label on icon-only buttons.
Set aria-current="page" on active pagination buttons.
Set explicit aria-label values on Previous/Next pagination controls.
Expose accurate aria-sort on sortable table headers.
Ensure checkbox controls have accessible labels with clear scope.
outOfScopeByDefault: Screen-reader narrative tuning beyond semantic correctness

notes: Feature-local components and hooks are allowed inside features/**.
Shared UI primitives belong in shared/ui/**, not src/components.
UI frameworks/component kits and infra belong in shared/** and must not live in features/**.
Documentation-only examples belong in docs/, not in src/features/**.

principles: Integration tests are the default for feature confidence.
Unit tests are limited to pure helpers only.

snapshots.policy: Snapshots are allowed but must remain minimal and human-reviewable; avoid DOM-tree snapshots.

mocking.policy: Mock only true externals (network/time/browser APIs/storage). Prefer MSW for API.
